questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Only then did the true cost of the merger become apparent.
Only then the true cost of the merger became apparent.
Only then became the true cost of the merger apparent did.
Only then the true cost of the merger did become apparent.
questions.explanation: Fronting 'only then' triggers inversion: 'Only then did the true cost become apparent.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: It was suggested that the manager review the contract personally.
It was suggested that the manager reviews the contract personally.
It was suggested that the manager will review the contract personally.
It was suggested that the manager reviewing the contract personally.
questions.explanation: After 'it was suggested that', formal English uses the subjunctive: 'the manager review the contract.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Supposing the deal collapses, what is the backup plan?
Supposing the deal collapse, what is the backup plan?
Supposed the deal collapses, what is the backup plan?
Supposing that the deal will collapse, what is the backup plan?
questions.explanation: 'Supposing' can introduce a hypothetical condition like 'if': 'Supposing the deal collapses, what is the plan?'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: For all that, the company remains a market leader.
For all of that, the company remains a market leader.
For all that, but the company remains a market leader.
For all it that, the company remains a market leader.
questions.explanation: 'For all that' is a fixed formal concessive phrase meaning 'despite everything': 'For all that, the company remains a leader.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: It is innovation that will determine the industry's future winners.
It innovation is that will determine the industry's future winners.
It is innovation which will determine the industry's future winners who.
It is innovation whom will determine the industry's future winners.
questions.explanation: Cleft sentences for emphasis on a non-personal subject use 'It is [thing] that...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The whistleblower alleges that funds were misappropriated.
The whistleblower alleges to that funds were misappropriated.
The whistleblower alleges funds being misappropriated.
The whistleblower is allege that funds were misappropriated.
questions.explanation: 'Allege' is followed by 'that + clause': 'alleges that funds were misappropriated.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Given that inflation remains high, the bank raised interest rates again.
Give that inflation remains high, the bank raised interest rates again.
Giving that inflation remains high, the bank raised interest rates again.
Given that inflation remaining high, the bank raised interest rates again.
questions.explanation: 'Given that' introduces a reason clause: 'Given that inflation remains high, the bank raised rates...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Only a fraction of shareholders has voted so far.
Only a fraction of shareholders have voted so far.
Only a fraction of shareholders is voted so far.
Only the fraction shareholders have voted so far.
questions.explanation: 'A fraction of' + plural noun usually takes a plural verb: 'a fraction of shareholders have voted.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The figures must have been miscalculated somewhere along the line.
The figures must been miscalculated somewhere along the line.
The figures must have miscalculate somewhere along the line.
The figures must have miscalculating somewhere along the line.
questions.explanation: 'Must have been + past participle' expresses a confident deduction about the past: 'must have been miscalculated.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Both the CEO and the CFO were questioned by regulators.
Both the CEO and the CFO was questioned by regulators.
Both the CEO or the CFO were questioned by regulators.
Both the CEO and did the CFO questioned by regulators.
questions.explanation: 'Both...and' takes a plural verb: 'Both the CEO and the CFO were questioned.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The merger was ostensibly aimed at cutting costs.
The merger was ostensible aimed at cutting costs.
The merger ostensibly was aimed at cutting costs it.
The merger was aimed ostensibly at cutting costs, that.
questions.explanation: 'Ostensibly' hedges a stated purpose, implying doubt: 'was ostensibly aimed at cutting costs.'

questions.topic: Advanced relative clauses (the extent to which)
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The report examines the extent to which automation has affected jobs.
The report examines the extent which automation has affected jobs to.
The report examines the extent to that automation has affected jobs.
The report examines to the extent which automation has affected jobs.
questions.explanation: 'The extent to which' is a formal relative structure: 'the extent to which automation has affected jobs.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Rarely, if ever, does the fund miss its quarterly target.
Rarely, if ever, the fund misses its quarterly target.
Rarely if ever the fund does miss its quarterly target.
Rarely, if ever, misses the fund its quarterly target does.
questions.explanation: 'Rarely, if ever' at the start triggers inversion: 'does the fund miss its quarterly target.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The disclosure of the accounting error triggered a share sell-off.
The disclose of the accounting error triggered a share sell-off.
The disclosure of the accounting error trigger a share sell-off.
The disclosing the accounting error triggered a share sell-off.
questions.explanation: Formal writing nominalizes verbs: 'disclose' becomes 'the disclosure of...'

questions.topic: Passive with modal perfect (may have been)
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The data may have been compromised during the breach.
The data may been compromised during the breach.
The data may have compromise during the breach.
The data may have being compromised during the breach.
questions.explanation: Modal perfect passive: modal + have been + past participle: 'may have been compromised.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The northern branch expanded; the southern, contracted.
The northern branch expanded; the southern expanded, contracted.
The northern branch expanded; the southern is contracted.
The northern branch expanded; the southern contracts already.
questions.explanation: Ellipsis omits the repeated verb after a semicolon: 'the southern, contracted' (= the southern branch contracted).

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Margins have narrowed. In other words, profitability is under pressure.
Margins have narrowed, in other words profitability is under pressure.
Margins have narrowed. In other words profitability is under pressure.
Margins have narrowed in other words, profitability is under pressure.
questions.explanation: 'In other words' begins a new sentence and is followed by a comma.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Irrespective of the outcome, the negotiations were valuable.
Irrespective the outcome, the negotiations were valuable.
Irrespective of the outcome, but the negotiations were valuable.
The outcome irrespective of, the negotiations were valuable.
questions.explanation: 'Irrespective of' is followed directly by a noun phrase: 'Irrespective of the outcome...'

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate formal opening line for an email apologizing for a delayed response?
options: Sorry it took forever to get back to you lol.
Please accept my apologies for the delay in responding to your enquiry.
My bad, I totally forgot to reply.
Ugh, sorry for the late reply.
questions.explanation: 'Please accept my apologies for the delay...' is a standard formal apology opening.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate opening line for a formal complaint about a cancelled contract?
options: I am writing to express my concern regarding the unilateral cancellation of our contract.
You cancelled our contract and that's totally unfair.
I am writing to express my concern regarding the unilateral cancellation of our contract, seriously.
This cancellation is outrageous and I demand an explanation right now.
questions.explanation: Formal complaints use precise, measured language such as 'I am writing to express my concern regarding...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The new leadership brought about significant cultural change.
The new leadership brought significant cultural change about of.
The new leadership brought about of significant cultural change.
The new leadership brought significant cultural change of about.
questions.explanation: 'Bring about' means 'to cause': 'brought about significant cultural change.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The board made its decision known through a formal statement.
The board made its decision know through a formal statement.
The board made known its decision through a formal statement it.
The board made its decision knowing through a formal statement.
questions.explanation: 'Make + object + past participle' shows the outcome of an action: 'made its decision known.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Barring unforeseen setbacks, the project will finish on schedule.
Barred unforeseen setbacks, the project will finish on schedule.
Bar unforeseen setbacks, the project will finish on schedule.
Barring unforeseen setbacks that, the project will finish on schedule.
questions.explanation: 'Barring' is a fixed absolute participle meaning 'except for, unless there are': 'Barring unforeseen setbacks...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: For the sake of transparency, the firm published its full accounts.
For the sake transparency, the firm published its full accounts.
For the sake of transparency that, the firm published its full accounts.
For sake of the transparency, the firm published its full accounts.
questions.explanation: 'For the sake of' means 'in order to achieve': 'For the sake of transparency, the firm published...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The fund incurred heavy losses during the downturn.
The fund suffered heavy losses incur during the downturn.
The fund made incur heavy losses during the downturn.
The fund incurred of heavy losses during the downturn.
questions.explanation: 'Incur losses' is a fixed collocation: 'the fund incurred heavy losses.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The agency has closely monitored the negotiations.
The agency has monitored closely the negotiations.
Closely the agency has monitored the negotiations.
The agency closely has monitored the negotiations.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of manner typically follow the auxiliary verb: 'has closely monitored.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Sales in Europe declined. On the other hand, Asian sales grew.
Sales in Europe declined, on the other hand Asian sales grew.
Sales in Europe declined. On the other hand Asian sales grew.
Sales in Europe declined on the other hand, Asian sales grew.
questions.explanation: 'On the other hand' begins a new sentence and is followed by a comma.

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: The panel would rarely overturn such a ruling, would it?
The panel would rarely overturn such a ruling, wouldn't it?
The panel would rarely overturn such a ruling, doesn't it?
The panel would rarely overturn such a ruling, does it?
questions.explanation: 'Rarely' makes the statement effectively negative, so the tag is positive: 'would rarely overturn..., would it?'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The turnaround was not entirely unexpected.
The turnaround was not all unexpected entirely.
The turnaround not was entirely unexpected.
The turnaround was entirely not unexpected.
questions.explanation: Formal understatement places 'not' before the adverb: 'was not entirely unexpected.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Should you require further information, please do not hesitate to contact us.
Should you requiring further information, please do not hesitate to contact us.
You should require further information, please do not hesitate to contact us.
Should you require further information, please not hesitate to contact us do.
questions.explanation: 'Should + subject + base verb' is a formal inverted conditional common in business correspondence: 'Should you require further information, please contact us.'
